description: I’m Marx, one guy disrupt all
summary:
Fire Memory Patagonia turns NASA MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections into a comparable calendar of thermal activity. Directly merging the Patagonian records produces an apparent 9.5-fold increase; harmonization reduces the recorded activity ratio to 1.8. Neither ratio measures unique fires or burned area.

The historical two-factor method was calibrated in northern Argentina in 2012–2018 and evaluated in Patagonia in 2019–2025. Predicted and observed Aqua totals differed by 2.1%; typical monthly error was a factor of 1.37 on months with at least five Aqua detections. This is retrospective evaluation: the static-source filter uses the full archive, and production factors were subsequently refitted.

An interactive calendar, area queries, downloads and a 3D observation atlas make the evidence accessible. Recorded satellite observation times, regional wind and dated news help explain the observations and their limitations. Regional reliability maps show where conversion fails.

Maps also include a history-based local adjustment; the historical validation figures apply to the base method, not that new adjustment. The intended benefit is clearer historical monitoring, not a demonstrated improvement in firefighting outcomes.
details:
THE PROBLEM

MODIS and VIIRS observe different pixel sizes and overpass times. Adding their detections directly can make an instrument change look like a large change in fire activity. Fire Memory expresses the historical record in MODIS-Aqua-equivalent hot spots and makes sampling limitations visible.

WHAT WE BUILT

The public app processes approximately 6.35 million NASA FIRMS detections over Argentina. It provides an English interface and a Spanish version, an area-and-period query, a year-by-month calendar, comparisons with historical medians, and CSV/PNG downloads. Its weekly regional context spans 23 fire seasons, 2002/03–2024/25.

A 3D atlas replays observed detection days, with historical regional wind and dated news for context. Smooth heat represents relative detection density, not temperature, burned area or a spread forecast. Satellite groups and news associations do not establish that every group is one confirmed incident. The satellite-clock viewer displays recorded local-solar observation times, not physical orbital tracking.

HOW IT WORKS

The base series uses separate daytime and nighttime conversion factors. Product flags, persistence and industrial-cell exclusions classify 36.6% of Patagonian VIIRS detections as static or industrial candidates. This is not a confirmed inventory of gas flares, and filtering can remove vegetation fire within industrial cells.

Maps and the area explorer now adjust the national factors by calendar month where a 0.5-degree cell has sufficient pre-2019 Aqua history; elsewhere they retain national factors. This local adjustment is reported separately: it has not inherited the base method's validation scores. Production national factors and static-source preprocessing use the full archive, so the displayed historical product is retrospective.

EVIDENCE

The base two-factor method was calibrated outside Patagonia in 2012–2018 and evaluated against Aqua observations in Patagonia in 2019–2025. The difference in the aggregate test total was 2.1%, while typical monthly error was a factor of 1.37 for months with at least five Aqua detections. The aggregate difference is not a percentage of correctly detected fires or a guarantee for each month, pixel or selected area.

A second evaluation withheld geographic blocks when fitting national factors and mapped regional disagreement. Some blocks, especially in southern Patagonia, had insufficient observations to judge. An independently implemented calculation using the same FIRMS snapshot checked the results; it was not an independent new dataset.

The project also measured known orbital timing changes in the Argentine record: in 2025, Terra's recorded daytime median was approximately 69 minutes earlier and Aqua's 68 minutes later than the 2012–2020 reference. Detection ratios changed too, but timing, sensitivity, geometry and processing were not fully separated. The app retains failed hypotheses and limitations rather than presenting every finding as a universal law.

INTENDED IMPACT AND LIMITS

A brigadista or monitoring team can ask whether activity is unusual for a location and season, inspect coverage and conversion limits, and download the evidence. These are intended monitoring benefits; improved operational firefighting outcomes have not been demonstrated. Hot spots are detections, not fire-event counts or burned area. Small fires before 2012 cannot be reconstructed. January–October 2026 is not loaded; November is a dated partial snapshot. The static app does not automatically refresh FIRMS. Regional daily wind is approximate context, not local gusts or proof of causation.

The downloadable public package contains the web client and exported data. The seven-slide demonstration presents the problem, historical test, local relevance, satellite-clock findings, validation criteria and intended use.

DATA AND RESOURCES

NASA FIRMS: MODIS Collection 6.1 active-fire detections from Terra and Aqua, and VIIRS 375 m detections from S-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21. The local Argentine archive covers 2000–2025 with a dated partial near-real-time snapshot in November 2026. FIRMS supplies the detections used for filtering, harmonization, calendars, observation trajectories and numerical evaluation.

NASA GIBS: corrected-reflectance imagery as a map layer.

NASA POWER: modeled daily weather/soil-moisture inputs for analyses and historical regional wind context; these are not measurements at each fire.

NASA Earth Observatory / Landsat–USGS: attributed Valle Magdalena imagery.

NASA Science Spacecraft Icons: official technical illustrations for the explanatory satellite-clock viewer.

The challenge was proposed by CONAE; we do not claim to use a CONAE data product. Other resources include Instituto Geográfico Nacional basemaps, OpenStreetMap contributors, Mapterhorn terrain and Natural Earth administrative outlines. Official national/provincial reports, park agencies and UNESCO provide dated news context. Links and attribution remain in the app. News context is not independent verification of every satellite group.

AI ASSISTANCE

Yes. We used Claude (Anthropic) and OpenAI Codex extensively as AI coding, analysis and writing assistants. They helped implement Python analyses, statistical checks, the HTML/CSS/JavaScript app, the 3D atlas, explanatory visualizations, coverage and export corrections, bilingual text, and attributed summaries of news reports.

The human team selected the challenge and region, set the project direction, reviewed evidence and decided what to retain. Separate AI agents were also instructed to challenge findings and independently check numerical calculations on the same dataset. Those checks do not constitute independent new observations or external validation.

Reported satellite counts and statistics come from executable analyses of NASA data, not values invented by a language model. The interface distinguishes measured observations, model-based conversions and illustrative graphics. Satellite imagery and technical spacecraft illustrations have attributed NASA sources. AI assistance is disclosed in the app and presentation.

AI HYPOTHESIS PROPOSER

A separate, authenticated Cloudflare Workers AI service uses Google Gemma 4 to draft falsifiable hypotheses from permitted Argentine training metadata and select from two previously frozen method families. It has no bindings to the sealed evaluation database or storage and receives no hidden reference observations. A successful real inference on 15 November 2026 returned a draft protocol with a verified SHA-256 hash. It did not register a protocol, query the sealed inputs or consume an evaluation. Human review and freezing remain required before any separate test. This component does not establish improved numerical accuracy. Public scope and inference receipt: https://fire-memory-patagonia.pages.dev/ai-proposer.html

IMPLEMENTATION

Python, NumPy and SciPy support the analyses. The public client uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript, Leaflet and MapLibre GL JS. Cloudflare Pages hosts the app; the AI proposer is a separate Cloudflare Worker. The public source download contains the web client and exported data; the private analytical engine is not included.

PUBLIC CLIENT AND EXPORTED DATA

https://fire-memory-patagonia.pages.dev/source-code.zip
